page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration operates with a dedicated CPU allocation and a single thread per physical core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the t2d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers with a stress-ng single-core score of 2688.09. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21511.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7817.0, both falling within the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 95.12 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 51.75 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Cryptographic and vector workloads are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, though the processor lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. However, tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and lack of hyperthreading, which limits parallel execution density compared to multi-threaded architectures. This instance is appropriate for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, software compilation, database operations, and light language model inference.
